Paragraph:
Translation: On the other hand, he who controls the senses by the mind and engages his active organs in works of devotion, without attachment, is by far superior.

Purport (Excerpt): Instead of becoming a pseudo-transcendentalist for the sake of wanton living... it is far better to remain in one's own business and execute the purpose of life... A householder can also reach this destination by regulated service... A sincere sweeper in the street is far better than the charlatan meditator who meditates only for the sake of making a living.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Determining what constitutes true integrity and effective personal progress in daily life.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna presents the ideal path: using a disciplined mind to direct physical actions toward selfless, dedicated work without emotional attachment. Krishna declares an honest worker superior to a pretentious renunciant.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna learns that active engagement in world duties with the right mindset is spiritually and mentally superior to false retreat.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Integrity Over Pretense: Choosing honest, practical work over a grand but false lifestyle
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Mindful Action: Engaging active organs in purposeful work without greedy attachment
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Internal Regulation: Directing external physical actions through a controlled intellect

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Karma-yoga (Engaging active organs in work without selfish attachment)
Asaktah (Unattached to personal rewards while performing duty)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: A sincere person who stays in their social role, regulates their senses, and offers their active work to the Lord without selfish attachment is vastly superior to a hypocritical renunciant. Active devotion within daily life is the genuine path to spiritual elevation.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Authentic, humble engagement in daily tasks with psychological alignment is far healthier than attempting grandiose lifestyles you are not mentally prepared for. A street sweeper acting with focus and integrity experiences more mental stability than an executive or guru who is internally chaotic and superficial.
